action: Check PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle Database and Oracle REST Data Services against the fixed versions in the vendor advisories and patch. Review which low-privilege database accounts exist.
date_note: Date of the Depthfirst research post (18 Nov); The Hacker News covered it on 19 Nov.
exec: Widely used databases have researcher-demonstrated chains that let limited-privilege accounts run code on the server. Vendors have fixes for all five flaws, so unpatched servers are the exposure.
plain: A researcher demonstrated that a database account with limited privileges can run code on the server in PostgreSQL, MySQL and other databases. Vendors have fixes for all five flaws.

key_findings: Researcher Zheng Yu of Depthfirst published proofs of concept for memory-corruption bugs in PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus an Oracle chain the researcher says needs no login; per The Hacker News, Oracle rates neither of the two Oracle flaws as exploitable without a login on its own.
Four flaws have vendor CVEs and fixes; ClickHouse has no CVE and was fixed in September (26.9 and later, with backports), per The Hacker News after its 20 Nov correction.
The article says no attack in the wild has been seen and the full chains were not reproduced independently.

summary: The Hacker News reports that Depthfirst researcher Zheng Yu demonstrated proof-of-concept chains letting limited-privilege accounts run code on PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse servers, plus an Oracle chain the researcher says needs no login; Oracle rates neither of its two flaws as exploitable without a login on its own. Four flaws have CVEs and fixes; ClickHouse, without a CVE, fixed its flaw in early September. No attacks are reported and the chains were not independently reproduced.
title: Researcher demonstrates database RCE exploit chains for PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle

validation.note: Compared Depthfirst's own post (18 Nov), Brandefense (19 Nov) and The Hacker News (19 Nov): researcher chains for PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle, same CVEs, vendor fixes for the CVE-listed flaws. ClickHouse having no CVE and being fixed in September is stated only by The Hacker News (summary attributes it); neither Depthfirst nor Brandefense says exploit code is public or that no attacks were seen.

review.note: Compared title, date (18 Nov Depthfirst post), four CVEs, Oracle no-login wording, ClickHouse Sept fix (THN 20 Nov correction), no-attacks and not-reproduced statements against Depthfirst, The Hacker News and Brandefense
